messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2989930
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1186/1754-1611-4-13

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: BioCoder-Formalized Plasmid DNA Extraction Protocol (Alkaline Lysis Miniprep, Excerpt, Figure 3)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Rich Medium (LB, YT, or Terrific medium containing appropriate antibiotic, 2 ml)
  - Bacteria Colony (a single colony of transformed bacteria)
  - Alkaline Lysis Solution I (50 mM Glucose, 25 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 10 mM EDTA pH 8.0, 100 ul)
  - Alkaline Lysis Solution II (freshly prepared, 0.2 N NaOH, 1% SDS w/v, 200 ul)
  - Alkaline Lysis Solution III (5 M sodium acetate, glacial acetic acid, 150 ul)

STEPS (as encoded in BioCoder, Figure 3; text output in Figure 4):
1. Preparation of cells: inoculate 2 ml Rich medium with a single colony of transformed bacteria; incubate with shaking for 12 hrs (overnight) at 37 C.
2. Measure out 1.5 ml of culture into a sterile 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube. Centrifuge at maximum speed for 30 secs at 4 C; gently aspirate out the supernatant and discard it (leave the pellet as dry as possible).
3. Lysis of Cells: add 100 ul of Alkaline Lysis Solution I; resuspend the pellet by vortexing or shaking vigorously.
4. Add 200 ul of freshly prepared Alkaline Lysis Solution II; close the tube tightly and invert 5 times (do not vortex); store the tube on ice.
5. Add 150 ul of Alkaline Lysis Solution III; close the tube tightly and gently mix the contents by inverting until the precipitate stops sticking to the walls of the tube; store the tube on ice for 3-5 mins.
6. Centrifuge at maximum speed for 5 mins at 4 C and aspirate out the top layer into a clean sterile microfuge tube; discard the bottom layer.
(Steps 7-13, phenol-chloroform extraction and ethanol precipitation, are omitted for brevity in the source paper itself.)

INTERPRETATION: This excerpt is used by the paper to demonstrate that a BioCoder program (46 lines of C++ instructions for the full protocol) can be automatically translated into both a human-readable, standardized English-language description (Figure 4) and a graphical task dependency visualization (Figure 5) equivalent in content to the original textbook protocol (from Molecular Cloning, Sambrook & Russell), while removing ambiguity around vague terms (e.g., disambiguating "mix" into a four-point intensity scale of tap/stir/invert/vortex) and separating essential instructions from non-essential comments (e.g., "leave the pellet as dry as possible" is treated as a comment, not an instruction).

ir.content:
main:
	medium1[0] = dispense(rich_medium)
	colony1[0] = dispense(bacteria_colony)
	culture1[0] = mix(medium1[0], colony1[0])
	heat(culture1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 43200.0SECOND
	sol11[0] = dispense(lysis_sol1)
	lysed11[0] = mix(culture1[0], sol11[0])
	sol21[0] = dispense(lysis_sol2)
	lysed21[0] = mix(lysed11[0], sol21[0])
	heat(lysed21[0]) @ 4.0CELSIUS @ 60.0SECOND
	sol31[0] = dispense(lysis_sol3)
	lysed31[0] = mix(lysed21[0], sol31[0])
	heat(lysed31[0]) @ 4.0CELSIUS @ 300.0SECOND
	dispose(lysed31[0])
	NOP

numeric_mismatches.note: BioScript has no centrifugation or phase-separation primitive, so pelleting/supernatant removal and top-layer aspiration are dropped from the executable sequence rather than approximated.

numeric_mismatches.field: heat ... at 4c used for ON_ICE storage
numeric_mismatches.note: BioScript has no dedicated store/wait primitive; the on-ice holds in steps 4 and 5 are approximated with 'heat' at 4 C, the nearest primitive exposing both a temperature and a duration, rather than a genuine storage construct. Step 4's indefinite ON_ICE hold (no duration given in the source) is assigned a short placeholder duration (1 min).
Not modeled. The source paper itself omits these steps (phenol-chloroform extraction and ethanol precipitation) for brevity, so there is no content to translate from them.
